knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper introduces RIDGE, a data analysis pipeline for triggered gravitational wave searches that leverages prior astronomical information and smaller data volumes to employ computationally expensive algorithms. The pipeline includes data conditioning using running median noise floor estimation and MBLT line removal, followed by a detection statistic based on regularized maximum likelihood.

attributes.description: Data analysis pipeline for triggered gravitational wave searches

attributes.prior_information: much more available than in un-triggered searches
attributes.sensitivity: higher than un-triggered searches due to reduced parameter space search volume

attributes.purpose: Estimate noise floor of power spectral density (PSD)
attributes.advantage: Ability to reject outliers such as narrowband noise artifacts

attributes.purpose: Line estimation and removal to reduce narrowband noise features
attributes.mechanism: Estimates amplitude and phase modulation of line features at a given carrier frequency

attributes.reason_for_regularization: Inverting detector responses to obtain polarization waveforms is an ill-posed problem

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text discusses the limited progress in using prior information for triggered gravitational wave searches, citing the SGR-1806-20 event as a notable example. It details the data conditioning process in the RIDGE pipeline, which uses a running median to estimate the noise floor and FIR filters for whitening, followed by MBLT for line noise removal.

attributes.status: limited advances in using prior information

attributes.model_basis: GWs from known pulsars in the Galaxy

attributes.description: data analysis pipeline for triggered searches

attributes.purpose: mitigate the effect of known instrumental artifacts

relationships.target: noise floor of the power spectral density (PSD)
running median estimate of the PSD
PSD from user-specified training data segment

attributes.timescale: shorter than the gap between training and processed data

attributes.effect: reduces or eliminates strong narrowband noise features (line noise)

relationships.target: power line interference or violin modes

knowledge_units.context_summary: The MBLT method estimates and removes line noise by tracking amplitude and phase modulation at a manually identified carrier frequency. It uses a running median to reject transient signals as outliers, ensuring they are not removed during the line subtraction process. The resulting whitened and line-removed data is then passed to the next stage of the RIDGE analysis pipeline.

relationships.target: amplitude and phase modulation of a line feature

attributes.reason: appear as outliers in amplitude/phase time series

attributes.description: data analysis pipeline for triggered searches

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes the regularization methods used in the RIDGE pipeline for coherent network analysis, noting that the hard constraint algorithm is a limit of the regulator used in reference [10]. It defines the sky-map output S(θ, φ) as the maximized likelihood over waveforms for a given sky location and introduces a detection statistic Rmm based on the ratio of maximum to minimum sky-map values.

attributes.role: basic algorithm for coherent network analysis in RIDGE

relationships.target: equal length, conditioned data segments from detectors in a given network
infinitely large gain factor for the regulator of [10]

attributes.definition: value of the likelihood of the data maximized over all possible h+ and h× waveforms with durations less than or equal to the data segments, as a function of θ and φ

attributes.formula: max_{θ,φ} S(θ, φ) / min_{θ,φ} S(θ, φ)
attributes.description: detection statistic representing the ratio of the maximum to minimum value of S(θ, φ) on the θ–φ plane

attributes.composition: two 4km LIGO interferometers and the 2km LIGO interferometer

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study defines a radial detection statistic, Rrad, based on the deviation of observed sky-map values from their noise-only ensemble average. Monte Carlo simulations using a LIGO-Virgo network evaluated the performance of Rrad and Rmm statistics with injected sine-Gaussian signals. The simulations utilized design sensitivity curves for detector noise and specific instrumental artifacts to characterize detection capabilities.

attributes.definition: Radial distance of observed values in a scaled (Rmm, max S) plane from the mean location in the absence of a signal
attributes.formula_components: max S, max S0, Rmm, min S0, max S0

attributes.definition: Ratio of the maximum to the minimum value of the sky-map S(theta, phi)
Ensemble average of sky-maps taken over realizations with no GW signals

attributes.purpose: Characterize performance of detection statistics Rmm and Rrad
attributes.network_composition: 4km LIGO detectors (H1, L1), 2km LIGO detector (H2), Virgo detector (V1)

relationships.target: Design sensitivity curves for LIGO and Virgo

attributes.phase_relationship: h_x(t) has an added phase of pi/2 relative to h_+(t)

attributes.definition: Square root of the integral of the sum of squared h_+(t) and h_x(t) waveforms over time

attributes.generation_method: White noise passed through FIR filters matching design curves

relationships.target: Design sensitivity curves for LIGO and Virgo

knowledge_units.context_summary: The RIDGE pipeline uses regularized maximum likelihood network analysis for triggered gravitational wave searches. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that the Rrad statistic outperforms the Rmm statistic in detection performance. A signal with an hrss of 5 × 10^-22 Hz^-1/2 is detected with approximately 62% probability at a false alarm rate of 2 × 10^-2 Hz.

attributes.description: Analysis pipeline implementing regularized maximum likelihood based network analysis for triggered searches
attributes.function: Serves as a platform for trying out new regulators and provides an independent check for results from other pipelines

relationships.target: regularized maximum likelihood based network analysis

attributes.description: Detection statistic incorporating information from the full sky-map
Naive detection statistic based on max/min ratio of sky-map values

attributes.purpose: Characterize performance of detection statistics Rmm and Rrad

knowledge_units.context_summary: The RIDGE pipeline is designed to reconstruct gravitational wave waveforms at arbitrary sky locations. Future work will integrate a specific waveform estimation method to assess the accuracy of derived astrophysical information.

attributes.function: reconstructs h+ and h× waveforms at arbitrary sky locations
